fact: A day on Venus lasts 243 Earth days, longer than its 225-day year, because the planet rotates so slowly.

source.title: Venus

fact: The English word "set" has more distinct dictionary definitions than any other word, filling roughly 60,000 words of entry in the OED.

source.title: Set (word)

fact: Honey found sealed in ancient Egyptian tombs is still edible thousands of years later, thanks to its low moisture and natural acidity.

source.title: Honey

fact: In 1947, engineers on Harvard's Mark II computer found a moth trapped in a relay and taped it into the logbook, coining "debugging".

source.title: Software bug

fact: The Baader-Meinhof phenomenon makes a word or idea you just noticed for the first time seem to suddenly appear everywhere afterward.

source.title: Frequency illusion

fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin by accident in 1928 after noticing mold had killed bacteria in a contaminated petri dish.

source.title: Alexander Fleming

fact: George Washington died in 1799, 25 years before scientists named the first dinosaur genus, Megalosaurus, in 1824, so he never knew dinosaurs had existed.

source.title: Megalosaurus

fact: In Italy, 17 is unlucky because its Roman numeral XVII is an anagram of VIXI, Latin for "I have lived" — implying "now I am dead." Many buildings skip a 17th floor, and Alitalia planes have no row 17.

source.title: Why 17 is Unlucky in Italy

fact: Finland sets speeding fines by income, not a flat rate. In 2002, a Nokia director paid a 116,000-euro fine for one offense, based on his multimillion-euro yearly income.

source.title: In Finland, speeding tickets are linked to your income

fact: Lyn Severance, who designed Ben & Jerry's original 1970s logo and lettering, was paid partly in free ice cream because the young company was short on cash.

source.title: Ben & Jerry's: The Inside Scoop: How Two Real Guys Built a Business with a Social Conscience and a Sense of Humor

fact: Only three people in the world can travel without a passport: the Emperor and Empress of Japan and the British monarch, all exempt due to their head-of-state status.

source.title: Only 3 People in the World Can Travel Without Passports, Who Are They?

fact: Most public hot springs in Japan ban visitors with tattoos. The rule began to keep out Yakuza members, who traditionally wear full-body tattoos.

source.title: Why Tattoos Are Avoided in Japanese Hot Springs

fact: Steamboat Willie, the 1928 cartoon that introduced Mickey Mouse, entered the US public domain on January 1, 2024, after its 95-year copyright term expired.

source.title: Steamboat Willie

fact: Marie Curie married Pierre Curie in 1895 wearing a plain navy dress instead of a wedding gown, then wore it as her lab coat for years afterward.

source.title: 10 Things You Might Not Know About Marie Curie

fact: A LEGO Master Model Builder's first training task is often to build a ball that does not fall apart, since a sphere is hard to make from rectangular bricks.

source.title: Instagram Reel

fact: In 1901, an Icelandic publisher translated Bram Stoker's Dracula as Makt Myrkranna, but secretly rewrote the plot and characters. No one noticed until a researcher compared the texts in 2014, over 100 years later.

source.title: Powers of Darkness (Iceland)

fact: On June 28, 2023, South Korea legally scrapped its traditional age system, where a baby turns 1 at birth and everyone gains a year every January 1. Overnight, most South Koreans became one or two years younger on paper.

source.title: Why are South Koreans suddenly younger? New age system explained

fact: In South Korea, people authenticate official documents with a carved personal stamp called a dojang instead of a handwritten signature, a practice that dates back to the 2nd century BCE.

source.title: Dojang: The Korean Name Stamp from History and Meaning to Where To Get One

fact: The Microsoft Excel World Championship has aired on ESPN, so competitors have appeared on the same network as elite athletes for building spreadsheet models.

source.title: Microsoft Excel World Championship

fact: IKEA names products instead of using numeric codes because founder Ingvar Kamprad was dyslexic and struggled to remember number sequences. Each category has its own naming source, such as Swedish lakes for bathroom items.

source.title: IKEA's Surprisingly Brilliant Product Branding Strategy

fact: An AI system built to sort pastries at Japanese bakeries was later adapted by a doctor to spot cancer cells on microscope slides, reaching about 99% accuracy.

source.title: The Pastry A.I. That Learned to Fight Cancer

fact: Amsterdam's canals swallow 12,000 to 15,000 bicycles a year. Divers also pull about 35 cars and 100 people out of the water each year.

source.title: How Many Bicycles and Cars End Up in Amsterdam's Canals?

fact: Cloudflare keeps a wall of 100 lava lamps in its San Francisco office. It films their random motion and feeds the footage into its encryption systems as a source of true randomness.

source.title: How Do Lava Lamps Help with Internet Encryption?

fact: Utrecht built the world's first fish doorbell: an underwater webcam at a canal lock lets anyone online press a button to alert a keeper when fish arrive and need help passing through.

source.title: The Dutch just gave the canal fish a 'fish doorbell' (no, we're not kidding)

fact: Starbucks holds over a billion dollars in unspent gift card and app balances at any time. Like a bank, it earns interest on that cash, and money that's never redeemed becomes pure profit.

source.title: How Starbucks is also a Bank?

fact: Starbucks took its name from Starbuck, the first mate on the whaling ship Pequod in Herman Melville's novel Moby-Dick. Founders chose it to evoke the romance and seafaring tradition of early coffee traders.

source.title: Our Name

fact: Britney Spears' song "...Baby One More Time" was originally titled "Hit Me Baby One More Time." Its Swedish songwriter thought "hit me" was American slang for "call me," not a request for violence.

source.title: We Finally Know What 'Hit Me, Baby, One More Time' Is Supposed To Mean

fact: France executed Hamida Djandoubi by guillotine on September 10, 1977, its last such execution, just months after Star Wars premiered. The guillotine was still France's official execution method at the time.

source.title: Hamida Djandoubi

fact: Nintendo was founded in Kyoto in 1889 as a playing-card company, the same year the Eiffel Tower opened in Paris and Jack the Ripper's identity was still unknown in London.

source.title: What do Nintendo and the Eiffel Tower Have in Common?

fact: Some Foley artists recreate movie rain by frying bacon or other food in a pan, but fact-checkers found this is only one of several techniques.

source.title: Digging into claim frying food is behind rain sounds in movies

fact: Mario's surname is officially "Mario." Nintendo creator Shigeru Miyamoto confirmed his full name is "Mario Mario," a naming convention that began with the 1993 live-action movie.

source.title: Miyamoto says Mario's full name is "Mario Mario"

fact: A group of ferrets is called a "business," a name that likely started as "busyness," describing how ferrets dart and scurry around like they are always up to something.

source.title: What's a Group of Ferrets Called?

fact: 17th-century Englishwoman Frances Wolfreston scrawled "frances wolfreston hor bouk" on every book she owned. Her copy of Shakespeare's 1593 poem Venus and Adonis is now the only one that survives.

source.title: Frances Wolfreston

fact: Every night at 11:57pm, over 90 digital billboards in Times Square pause their ads for three minutes to show a single artwork, a program called Midnight Moment.

source.title: Times Square Arts Midnight Moments

fact: WinRAR still runs its file-compression trial that never expires, yet public estimates put its annual revenue at just $4.8 million, earned by a team of only 15 people.

source.title: WinRAR - $4.8 M Revenue, Employees & Growth | Kona Equity

fact: Apple has an unwritten rule that movie villains never use iPhones on screen. Director Rian Johnson said Apple insists its products appear only in a positive light, so antagonists use other phones instead.

source.title: Here's Why You'll Never See Movie Villains Use iPhones

fact: When a single chip failed aboard Voyager 1 in 2023, NASA engineers restored contact by moving its code to other memory, fixing the probe from over 24 billion kilometers away.

source.title: How scientists fixed Voyager 1 at the edge of the Solar System

fact: Rome digs its metro tunnels 100 feet underground to avoid ancient ruins, but stations still hit history: workers found Emperor Hadrian's 2nd-century auditorium mid-construction, forcing planners to move a station entrance.

source.title: Rome's Rich Past Stalls Metro Line Expansion

fact: In 1975, physicist Jack Hetherington listed his cat as co-author of a physics paper, crediting him as F.D.C. Willard, after writing the whole paper using "we" and "our."

source.title: A cat co-authored an influential physics paper

fact: Movie credit terms like "with," "featuring," and "starring" carry different meanings. Actors' agents negotiate which word appears in the contract.

source.title: What Does "With" Mean in Acting Credits?

fact: In 2022, retired engineer David Smith discovered the "hat," a 13-sided shape that tiles a plane forever without repeating a pattern, the first single shape known to do this.

source.title: Newfound Mathematical 'Einstein' Shape Creates a Never-Repeating Pattern

fact: South Korea has required smartphones to make an audible camera shutter sound since 2004, with no way to mute it, to deter secret photography.

source.title: Korean Smartphones Have Mandatory Shutter Sounds, 8 in 10 Want it Muted

fact: The lemon likely originated in the Assam region of northeast India, though its exact birthplace is unknown. A genomic study found it isn't a wild species; it's a natural hybrid of the bitter orange and the citron.

source.title: Lemon

fact: John Pemberton invented Coca-Cola in 1886 while trying to cure his morphine addiction, which began after a saber wound in the Civil War.

source.title: John Stith Pemberton

fact: The Night's Watch cloaks in Game of Thrones, including Jon Snow's, were cut and shaved IKEA fur rugs with leather straps added, costume designer Michele Clapton revealed.

source.title: Game of Thrones uses IKEA rugs to make Night's Watch cloaks

fact: For Apple TV+'s Mythic Quest, Ubisoft's Red Storm studio built real, playable segments of the show's fictional game so actors could play them on set to inform their performances.

source.title: 'Mythic Quest': How Ubisoft Created the Fake Video Game at Center of Apple+ Comedy

fact: Estcourt Station, Maine, sits on the US-Canada border. Its only border crossing closes from 5 p.m. Friday to 8 a.m. Monday, so residents who leave during that time cannot legally return until it opens again.

source.title: Estcourt Station, Maine

fact: Iceland marks First Day of Summer as a public holiday every year, on the first Thursday after April 18. Schools and many offices close, and towns hold parades and flag-waving to celebrate.

source.title: The First Day of Summer in Iceland

fact: A kangaroo word hides a shorter synonym inside its own letters, in the same order. For example, "masculine" contains "male," and "chocolate" contains "cocoa."

source.title: Kangaroo word

fact: Platypuses glow an eerie blue-green under ultraviolet light, a trait called biofluorescence that scientists only discovered recently.

source.title: Platypuses glow an eerie blue-green under UV light

fact: Modern Windows stores its boot-screen spinner as a font, not a video. Each frame sits as a hidden character in the Segoe Boot Semilight font, saving power during startup.

source.title: The Windows 11 boot screen spinning circle is stored as a font

fact: The Bulwer-Lytton Fiction Contest, which invites entrants to write intentionally terrible opening sentences, ran for 42 years before founder Scott Rice retired it in July 2025.

source.title: The Bulwer-Lytton Fiction Contest

fact: Satellite images of a remote Chinese desert show a giant, detailed scale model of the disputed China-India border region, likely built for military planning and training.

source.title: Calibration Targets 3: China - Google Earth Blog

fact: Hermès heir Nicolas Puech, worth about $13 billion, sought to legally adopt his 51-year-old former gardener as an adult son so he could inherit part of the fortune instead of Puech's own charitable foundation.

source.title: Nicolas Puech: Hermes billionaire wants to bequeath fortune to his former gardener

fact: For Interstellar, Christopher Nolan planted 500 acres of real corn near Calgary instead of using CGI for the farm scenes, then sold the crop afterward and turned a profit.

source.title: How Christopher Nolan grew his own cornfield for Interstellar

fact: The word "gargoyle" comes from Old French "gargouille", meaning throat, an onomatopoeic root that also gave English the word "gargle".

source.title: Gargoyle - Etymology, Origin & Meaning

fact: Japan's teenage Emperor Uda wrote a diary entry in 889 CE praising his ink-black cat, now seen as the first confirmed record of a cat in Japan.

source.title: Ancient Diary from Emperor in Japan Sounds Like All Cat Lovers Today

fact: A nearly straight sailing route runs from the UK to New Zealand without crossing any land, curving only slightly around South America's southern tip.

source.title: You can sail from Britain to NZ in a straight line, new map shows

fact: Human lungs can absorb oxygen from certain liquids, not just air. Doctors used oxygen-rich perfluorocarbon liquid to ventilate premature infants' lungs in the 1990s.

source.title: Liquid breathing

fact: Ancient papyrus books were roughly square, shaped by how papyrus sheets were made. Medieval parchment, cut from rectangular animal skins, shifted books to that shape. Paper let books be any shape, but they kept those inherited proportions.

source.title: Why Books Evolved From Square to Rectangular Shape

fact: The most deeply nested island known sits in Lake Yathkyed, Canada: an island in a lake on an island in a lake on an island in a lake on an island. Geographers call it a fourth-order island.

source.title: Recursive islands and lakes

fact: In Casablanca Chess, games start not from the usual opening but from a real position taken from a famous historical game, between its 6th and 15th move. The variant debuted at a 2024 tournament in Morocco, won by Magnus Carlsen.

source.title: Casablanca Chess: A Stunning New Variant

fact: A calorie is a unit of heat, not mass. Food's calorie count was originally found by burning a dried sample in a calorimeter and measuring how much it heated a surrounding water bath.

source.title: How is the caloric value of food determined?

fact: Indium is a soft, inert, nontoxic metal that lets out a high-pitched cry when you bend it. The sound comes from crystal twinning as the metal's internal structure realigns under stress.

source.title: https://www.reddit.com/r/Damnthatsinteresting/comments/vojdv1/indium_is_a_inert_nontoxic_metal_which_is_very/

fact: While studying for his 1947 US citizenship exam, Kurt Gödel found a flaw in the Constitution he believed could let it turn into a dictatorship, but he never published what it was.

source.title: Gödel's Loophole

fact: On June 26, 1974, a supermarket in Troy, Ohio scanned a pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum as the first item ever read by a UPC barcode scanner.

source.title: Pack of chewing gum becomes first-ever item scanned with a UPC barcode | June 26, 1974 | HISTORY

fact: Switzerland's EMBAG law now requires all federal agencies to release the source code of software built for them as open source, unless security or third-party rights prevent it.

source.title: Switzerland now requires all government software to be open source

fact: The costume designer for Idiocracy (2006) put background actors in Crocs because they were cheap and seemed too ugly to ever catch on. A two-year release delay meant Crocs went mainstream right as the film hit theaters.

source.title: Everyone in 'Idiocracy' Wears Crocs Because They Were 'Horrible' and Cheap?

fact: Oranges are often sold in red mesh bags because of the Munker illusion: red lines overlaid on the orange skin trick the brain into seeing the fruit as brighter and fresher than it is.

source.title: The Reason Why Oranges Are Sold in Red Mesh Bags

fact: Cymatics is the science of making sound visible: sound waves sent through sand, water, or a metal plate arrange the medium into intricate, symmetric patterns that shift with the frequency.

source.title: Cymatics: The Visualization of Sound

fact: New Zealander Nigel Richards won the French-language World Scrabble Championship in 2015 and 2018 despite not speaking or understanding French, having memorized the French dictionary.

source.title: Nigel Richards

fact: Philippine gymnast Carlos Yulo's two 2024 Olympic golds earned him a $415,000 condo, over $225,000 in government cash, and lifetime perks like free ramen, buffets, and even free colonoscopies starting at 45.

source.title: Philippines gold medal gymnast Carlos Yulo to receive house, cash, free ramen for life

fact: Brad Pitt agreed to cameo in Deadpool 2 as a favor, joking he only wanted a cup of coffee in return. Ryan Reynolds later repaid him with a matching cameo in Bullet Train.

source.title: Bullet Train: Ryan Reynolds' Hilarious Cameo Was To Pay Back Brad Pitt

fact: Harvard was founded in 1636, before calculus existed. Newton and Leibniz developed calculus in the 1660s-1680s, and Harvard did not teach it until the 1720s, nearly 90 years later.

source.title: Harvard is older than calculus.

fact: Teaching began at the University of Oxford by 1096, more than two centuries before the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.

source.title: The University of Oxford Is Older Than the Aztec Empire and Other Facts That Will Change Your Perspective on History

fact: A photo finish isn't a snapshot of a moment. The camera stares at one fixed line on the track and stitches together everything that crosses it over time, frame by frame.

source.title: How are photo finishes determined?

fact: One theory traces "let the cat out of the bag" to an old scam: sellers swapped a cheap cat for a suckling pig in a sealed sack, hidden until the buyer opened it. A 1530 letter from Johannes Agricola to Martin Luther already used the phrase.

source.title: Letting the cat out of the bag

fact: Farfetch'd's Japanese name, Kamonegi, comes from a Japanese idiom for an unlikely stroke of luck: a duck arriving already carrying the green onions needed for duck stew.

source.title: On the Origin of Species: Farfetch'd

fact: English had no word for the color orange until around 1510, when it was named after the fruit. Before that, the color was called "yellow-red," and since "redhead" was already in use, it stuck for orange-haired people too.

source.title: Orange (word)

fact: The word "boycott" comes from Charles Boycott, an 1880s Irish land agent whom tenant farmers shunned. A priest suggested calling the tactic "to Boycott him," and the name became a verb.

source.title: Charles Boycott

fact: "Dude" once meant the opposite of a laid-back surfer — in the 1880s it was an insult for an over-dressed city man, and cowboys used it to mock Easterners in fancy store-bought clothes. It likely comes from the "doodle" of "Yankee Doodle Dandy."

source.title: Dude

fact: NASA's "Your Name in Landsat" tool spells out your name using real satellite photos of Earth, matching each letter to a landform or terrain feature shaped like it.

source.title: Your Name in Landsat

fact: The idiom "cut to the chase" comes from silent-film script directions, first written in the 1929 novel Hollywood Girl. It told editors to skip straight to the chase scene that closed most films of the era.

source.title: https://knowyourphrase.com/cut-to-the-chase

fact: Human saliva contains opiorphin, a natural peptide that in rat tests blocked acute pain up to six times more strongly than morphine.

source.title: Human Opiorphin, a natural antinociceptive modulator of opioid-dependent pathways

fact: American Zachariah Swope watched 777 different movies in cinemas over one year, from July 2022 to June 2023, a Guinness World Record. He used a Regal Cinemas subscription to raise awareness for autism and suicide prevention.

source.title: Most films seen in a cinema in one year

fact: Every book shares the same fake country of origin: the ISBN prefix 978 (later also 979), nicknamed "Bookland." It exists only inside the EAN barcode system, letting books worldwide use one shared numbering scheme.

source.title: Bookland

fact: Color laser printers secretly print a grid of near-invisible yellow dots encoding their serial number and the date and time. These hidden tracking dots helped identify NSA leaker Reality Winner in 2017.

source.title: Printer tracking dots

fact: Amsterdam residents tape off one-square-meter patches of pavement each spring to claim a personal 'sun spot' for sunbathing, picnics, and inflatable pools. The city reclaims the spots every October for winter bike parking.

source.title: https://www.instagram.com/reels/DIwT_4bodBb/

fact: In the UK, millions of viewers switching on kettles during TV ad breaks spikes national electricity demand, an effect called TV pickup. The largest recorded spike, 2,800 megawatts, followed England's 1990 World Cup penalty shootout loss.

source.title: TV pickup

fact: A star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame costs $85,000, a sponsorship fee covering its production, installation, and upkeep, usually paid by a studio or sponsor rather than the celebrity.

source.title: People are only just discovering the ridiculous amount celebrities have to pay to get a star on the Walk of Fame

fact: A deep sea trench called Beaufort's Dyke, in the North Channel between the UK and Ireland, holds about a million tons of WWII-era munitions the UK dumped there, including chemical weapons, making seabed drilling there hazardous.

source.title: Beaufort's Dyke

fact: Most wasabi served outside Japan is not real wasabi. It is horseradish mixed with mustard powder and green food coloring, since true wasabi is hard to grow.

source.title: https://www.theatlantic.com/video/index/585172/wasabi-fake/

fact: The modern stock market began in the Netherlands. In 1602, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) sold shares to the public to spread the risk of its costly spice voyages to Asia.

source.title: VOC: the start of global share trading

fact: In Japan, only 100% fruit juice may show a cut fruit cross-section on the label. Drinks with 5-99% juice may show a whole fruit, and drinks under 5% juice may show no realistic fruit image at all.

source.title: Juice's Label

fact: Under a 1962 Japanese law against misleading packaging, snacks, cookies, and meals must closely match the shape, size, color, and topping placement shown on their packaging photos.

source.title: The Japanese Food Packaging Rule That Guarantees What You See Is What You Get

fact: The QWERTY effect claims words typed with more letters from the right side of the keyboard get rated slightly more positive than words leaning left, though the finding stays small and disputed.

source.title: Qwerty effect

fact: One theory says Venetian glassblowers turned a flawed masterpiece into an ordinary bottle, or fiasco. Some believe that downgrade from art to bottle is why fiasco came to mean a complete failure, though etymologists call the origin unconfirmed.

source.title: Fiasco: Italian Theatre Origins of Failure and Breakdown

fact: In a 2007 BMJ poll, more than 11,300 readers voted sanitation and sewage systems the greatest medical advance since 1840, ranking it above antibiotics and anesthesia.

source.title: BMJ readers choose the "sanitary revolution" as greatest medical advance since 1840

fact: 17th-century swordswoman and opera singer Julie d'Aubigny helped her lover fake death to flee a convent, stealing a corpse, setting a room on fire, and getting sentenced to death in absentia for kidnapping, arson, and body snatching.

source.title: Julie d'Aubigny

fact: A popular legend says a military statue's raised horse legs reveal how the rider died, but the code is mostly myth. Andrew Jackson's 1853 statue shows two raised legs, which the legend says means death in battle, though he died of tuberculosis.

source.title: Decoding Military Horse Statues

fact: The Home Alone house's exterior is a real home in Winnetka, Illinois, but its interior rooms were rebuilt full-size in a nearby high school gym for easier filming and lighting.

source.title: People Are Surprised That the Interior House Scenes of 'Home Alone' Were Filmed in a High School Gym

fact: The name Tiffany comes from Theophania and was used in England and France since medieval times. Historical novelists still avoid it, since readers assume it's a modern name, a bias called the "Tiffany problem."

source.title: Tiffany problem

fact: Activision CEO Bobby Kotick said the Aerosmith edition of Guitar Hero earned the band more money than any of their studio albums, through game sales, concert ticket sales, and new recording deals.

source.title: Aerosmith made more money on Guitar Hero than from any of their albums

fact: WWE star John Cena holds the Guinness World Record for most wishes granted through the Make-A-Wish Foundation, with over 650 wishes granted since 2002.

source.title: Most wishes granted through the Make-A-Wish Foundation

fact: France's longest land border with another country isn't in Europe. It runs about 730 km (454 miles) between French Guiana and Brazil, longer than France's border with Spain.

source.title: Brazil–France border

fact: Mongolian princess Khutulun never lost a wrestling match against a suitor, and each loser had to give her horses, so by her mid-twenties she owned over 10,000 of them.

source.title: Khutulun

fact: Universal Studios sued Nintendo in 1982, claiming Donkey Kong copied King Kong. Nintendo's lawyer John Kirby won by proving Universal did not own the King Kong rights, and Nintendo later named its character Kirby after him.

source.title: John Kirby (attorney)

fact: Poseidon fathered more named children than any other Greek god, with well over 100 recorded across various myths.

source.title: Poseidon Family Tree: The Divine Lineage of the Ancient Greek God of the Sea

fact: The US Air Force built the Condor Cluster in 2010 by linking 1,760 Sony PlayStation 3 consoles, reaching 500 trillion calculations per second at a fraction of normal supercomputer cost.

source.title: US Air Force connects 1,760 PlayStation 3's to build supercomputer

fact: Granny Smith apples are named after a real woman. Maria Ann "Granny" Smith grew the first tree in Australia around 1868, after a chance seedling sprouted from crab apple scraps she tossed out while baking a pie.

source.title: Granny Smith

fact: In 1975, actress Tippi Hedren taught 20 Vietnamese refugee women to do manicures. That small class grew into a nail salon industry now worth billions and run largely by Vietnamese Americans.

source.title: How Tippi Hedren made Vietnamese refugees into nail salon magnates

fact: US highways follow a grid system: even numbers run east-west and odd numbers run north-south. AASHTO coordinates the rules, which differ slightly between the older US Route system and the newer Interstate Highway system.

source.title: United States Numbered Highway System

fact:
Brightest aerial image formed by multirotors/drones
The brightest aerial image formed by multirotors/drones is 222,448.61 lux, and was achieved by Amazon MGM Studios (USA) with the support of Heads in the Sky in Los Angeles, California, USA on 19 May 2026.
